title: Onlookers foresee the fall of Mughal rule

blocks.text: As Taru Singh's scalp is scraped, he endures the pain without a cry, while the crowd recoils at the spectacle. The scene becomes a public indictment of the Nawab rather than a humiliation of the prisoner.

Witnesses openly say that The rule of the Mughals would not last long after such an outrage against a holy Singh. The page also records the shock felt across religious lines, showing that even many observers recognized the act as a violation that invited judgment.

The Nawab nevertheless keeps pressing Taru Singh, trying to mock his earlier claim that his hair could not be taken apart from his head. Instead of weakening him, the torture only deepens the sense that prophecy is about to answer imperial violence.
